slot.label: Describe what you want made
slot.hint2: — or just type the first letter of what you need.
slot.unwired: The generator is not connected to this build. Your request was not sent anywhere.
dep.head: What left the board today
dep.sub: Authored examples, not live traffic. Nothing has launched yet, so nothing here is a customer, a case study, or a number we are asking you to believe.
how.head: You are already halfway through the sentence
how.1.p: Twelve addresses, twelve things. Typing one into the bar is the first half of the request, so the board is already set before you have touched anything.
how.2.p: One line, your own words, in whichever of the ninety-nine languages you think in. No prompt craft, no template picker, no onboarding.
how.3.p: The destination, the pending change and the state are all on the board before anything is finished. A machine that shows its work is a machine you can stop.
how.4.p: Files, code, copy, infrastructure — the thing itself, not a preview of it and not a brief for someone else to build.
dest.head: Twelve destinations, one machine
dest.sub: Every address runs this same board. Pick a row and the whole page retimes to it — the lamp, the wheel, the slot, the example. That retiming is the product, not a demonstration of it.
spec.head: What actually comes out
spec.sub: One run, its manifest, and a real excerpt from it — including the parts where the machine says what it will not do.
lang.head: The board speaks your language, correctly
lang.sub: Not a machine-translated marketing page. The noun itself, in the right case, with the plural rules each language really uses — Arabic has six categories, Polish three, Japanese one. A pack that carries English's two into either is not partly translated, it is broken.
close.head: So. What do you want made?
close.sub: The wheel is still turning. Stop it wherever you like.
foot.note: One codebase serves all twelve addresses; the hostname is the entire configuration. Translations come from a shared dictionary of ninety-nine languages and ship as static packs, never fetched at runtime.
foot.honest: What this page does not claim
foot.honest.note: No customers, no ratings, no prices, no benchmarks. Every example here is authored and labelled. When there is real proof, it will replace them.
langboard.head: Language · 99 in the dictionary
line.website: Describe the site. Get the site — pages, copy, images, and the code behind them.
line.codes: Describe the behaviour. Get working code, its tests, and the reason it is written that way.
line.software: Describe what it should do for whom. Get a running application, not a repository to finish yourself.
line.cloud: Describe the load and the budget. Get infrastructure as code, with the failure modes written down.
line.email: Describe the news and the reader. Get the email — subject lines, plain text, and the HTML that renders everywhere.
line.team: Describe the work. Get a set of agents with defined roles that hand work to each other.
line.club: Describe who gathers and why. Get the members' space — joining, rooms, roll call, and the rules.
line.expert: Describe the question you keep asking. Get an adviser grounded in your own documents.
line.agency: Describe the client and the deadline. Get the studio — brief, identity, site, and the deck that sells it.
line.boutique: Describe the goods. Get the shop — product pages, photography, checkout, and the words that sell them.
line.services: Describe the work and how people book it. Get the booking, the quotes, the schedule, and the site that sells them.
line.support: Describe your product and your patience. Get a help desk that answers, escalates, and admits what it does not know.
